universe_policy.survivorship_note: Research breadth universe: 505 members = 501 stocks tracking the S&P 500 constituents + 4 index ETFs (SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA). Originally ~105 members tracking the S&P 100 (selected 2026-06-16 from today's survivors); expanded to the S&P 500 on 2026-06-21 by tools/expand_universe_sp500.py for experiment #1's breadth arm. ONE ISSUER PER MEMBER: where a company lists two share classes the redundant one is dropped and the Class A / more liquid ticker retained - GOOGL over GOOG, FOXA over FOX, NWSA over NWS. This deviates from the S&P 500 constituent list on purpose, because this is a cross-sectional research universe and not an index tracker: two near-identical series for one company would take two slots in any top-N ranking and inject near-collinearity into residualisation and beta estimation. The S&P 100 selection made this call for GOOG; the S&P 500 merge silently re-added it (and FOX/NWS) until 2026-08-06. MSTR is retained as a liquid survivor carried over from the live watchlist. 'membership_as_of' deliberately remains 2026-06-16 (the pre-expansion snapshot date) because with_min_history anchors its cutoff to that field - it is a computed value, not a label, so moving it would shift a filter. This is a forward-looking selection over the backtested history: it carries survivorship/selection bias because names that crashed, shrank, were acquired or delisted never enter the sample, and later listings carry shorter history (only GEV, PLTR and UBER carry a 'listed' date, so min_history filtering sees just those three - the remaining 498 stocks are unbounded on that axis). PIT constituent membership was deliberately NOT scraped (gap-map decision #6: bound the claim, do not chase paywalled delisted-price history). Bound every cross-sectional result to this fixed membership; do not extrapolate beyond it.
